title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Certain Issues Concerning the Application of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations (I)

articles.content_en: Article 2 For a foreign-related civil relation that arose before the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations came into force, the People's Court shall determine the applicable law in accordance with the relevant legal provisions in force at the time when the foreign-related civil relation arose; where there were no provisions in the laws at that time, the provisions of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations may be applied by reference.

Article 3 Where the provisions on the application of law to the same foreign-related civil relation in the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations and other laws are inconsistent, the provisions of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations shall apply, except for the special provisions of commercial area laws such as the Negotiable Instruments Law of the People's Republic of China, the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China, and the Civil Aviation Law of the People's Republic of China, as well as the special provisions of intellectual property area laws.
Where the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations has no provisions on the application of law to a foreign-related civil relation, but other laws have provisions, the provisions of other laws shall apply.

Article 4 Where the laws of the People's Republic of China do not explicitly provide that the parties may choose the law applicable to a foreign-related civil relation, and the parties choose to apply a law, the People's Court shall determine that such choice is invalid.

Article 5 Where one party claims that the choice is invalid on the ground that the law chosen by agreement of both parties has no actual connection with the disputed foreign-related civil relation, the People's Court shall not support such claim.

Article 6 Where the parties agree to choose or change the choice of applicable law before the conclusion of the court debate in the first instance, the People's Court shall permit it.
Where all parties invoke the law of the same country and raise no objection to the application of law, the People's Court may determine that the parties have made a choice of the law applicable to the foreign-related civil relation.

Article 7 Where the parties invoke in a contract an international treaty that has not yet taken effect for the People's Republic of China, the People's Court may determine the rights and obligations between the parties in accordance with the content of that international treaty, except where doing so violates the public interest of the People's Republic of China or the mandatory provisions of the laws and administrative regulations of the People's Republic of China.

Article 9 Where one party intentionally creates a connecting point for a foreign-related civil relation to circumvent the mandatory provisions of the laws and administrative regulations of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court shall determine that such act does not produce the effect of applying foreign law.

Article 10 Where the resolution of a foreign-related civil dispute requires the confirmation of another foreign-related civil relation as a prerequisite, the People's Court shall determine the law applicable to that preliminary question in accordance with its own nature.
Article 11 Where a case involves two or more foreign-related civil relations, the People's Court shall separately determine the law that shall be applicable.

Article 12 Where the parties have not chosen the law applicable to a foreign-related arbitration agreement, and have not agreed on the arbitration institution or the place of arbitration, or the agreement is unclear, the People's Court may apply the laws of the People's Republic of China to determine the validity of the arbitration agreement.

Article 13 Where a natural person has continuously resided for more than one year in a place that serves as the center of his or her life at the time of the creation, change or termination of a foreign-related civil relation, the People's Court may determine that place as the habitual residence of the natural person as prescribed in the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations, except for circumstances such as medical treatment, labor dispatch, or official duties.

Article 14 The People's Court shall determine the place of incorporation registration of a legal person as the place of registration of the legal person as prescribed in the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations.

Article 15 Where the People's Court still cannot obtain the foreign law through reasonable means such as provision by the parties, the channels prescribed in international treaties that have taken effect for the People's Republic of China, or provision by Chinese and foreign legal experts, it may be determined that the foreign law cannot be ascertained.
According to the provisions of Article 10, paragraph 1 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations, the parties shall provide the foreign law. Where the parties fail to provide the foreign law within a reasonable time limit designated by the People's Court without justifiable reasons, it may be determined that the foreign law cannot be ascertained.

Article 16 The People's Court shall hear the opinions of all parties on the content of the foreign law that shall be applied and its understanding and application. Where the parties have no objection to the content of the foreign law and its understanding and application, the People's Court may confirm it; where the parties have objections, the People's Court shall examine and determine it.

Article 17 For issues concerning the application of law to civil relations involving the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and the Macao Special Administrative Region, these Provisions shall be applied by reference.

Article 18 For cases of foreign-related civil disputes that arise after the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations comes into force, and for which a final judgment has not been rendered after this Interpretation comes into force, this Interpretation shall apply; for cases where a final judgment has been rendered before this Interpretation comes into force and the parties apply for retrial or a retrial is decided in accordance with the procedure for trial supervision, this Interpretation shall not apply.
Article 19 Where the judicial interpretations previously issued by this Court are inconsistent with this Interpretation, this Interpretation shall prevail.
